transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-25
Time: 11:00 AM PT / 19:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Monroe (Redwood AE), Sonia Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Priya Nair (Bramble Tech), Marco Alvarez (Platform), Evelyn Chow (Security)

Summary (auto): Quick handoff to cover security constraints and pilot scope. Action items captured at end.

00:00 Alex Monroe: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex, I'm the AE on the account. Quick intro, Sonia is our SE, Jordan's our CSM. How's everyone doing?
00:07 Priya Nair: Hey Alex, good thanks. Excited to get this rolling, we had a lot of internal alignment this week so should be able to move fast.
00:12 Alex Monroe: Awesome. The goal for today is a tight handoff so we can kick the pilot next week. I want to confirm constraints — security, network windows, and success criteria.
00:24 Sonia Patel: I'll mostly cover the technical setup and the benchmark plan. Quick note: Bramble mentioned a private deployment earlier — is that still the plan?
00:33 Marco Alvarez: Yes, private deployment. Prefer VPC peering into our account if possible. On-prem is too heavy right now.
00:40 Sonia Patel: Great, so we'll target Redwood Private (VPC). We'll need CIDR ranges and firewall egress rules — usually a set of outbound ports and allowlist for our control plane and inference endpoints.
00:51 Marco Alvarez: Understood, I'll pull the CIDR and route table info. Question — do you require full peering or is a proxy NAT acceptable?
01:01 Sonia Patel: Both are supported. Peering gives lowest latency. A NAT/proxy is fine for initial validation if you have strict infra policies — just expect higher latency and maybe extra hops for logs.
01:14 Evelyn Chow: On the security side, we need to confirm encryption in transit + at rest, KMS integration, and audit log retention. Also curious about where audit logs are stored and if they're accessible from our SIEM.
01:26 Alex Monroe: Yes, KMS integrations are supported — we can plug into your AWS KMS or you can use our managed keys. Logs can be streamed via S3 or to your logging endpoint. We'll send the SOC2 and security pack after the call.
01:39 Priya Nair: Which option is recommended for regulated data? We have some PII in training prompts but will RTP redact, but still need to comply.
01:47 Jordan Lee: For regulated workloads we usually recommend customer-managed KMS + VPC with private endpoints. That gives you control over keys and network. Also, set retention to minimum required by policy.
01:59 Priya Nair: Okay that sounds reasonable.
02:05 Sonia Patel: For the pilot we propose a minimal config: single model variant pinned, reserved instance sizes small (test pool), with autoscaling disabled for baseline. We'll run a sample traffic pattern — bursts and steady — to capture latency P95 and token costs.
02:23 Priya Nair: What's realistic for latency targets? We want sub 300 ms P95 for short prompts (~64 tokens) if possible.
02:32 Sonia Patel: On GPU-backed models with VPC peering, sub 300 ms P95 is plausible for 64-token generations depending on model choice. If you use a quantized variant on x86 or lower-end GPUs we might see 350–500 ms. We'll include model recommendations in the benchmark doc.
02:50 Marco Alvarez: We'll probably want a lighter open model to start — cost is a major factor.
02:56 Alex Monroe: Makes sense. One of the core Redwood differentiators is the cost/perf tooling — Optimize will suggest batching/quantization once we see the trace.
03:10 Evelyn Chow: About logs and auditability — does Redwood expose per-token metadata for tracing back queries? We need to attribute actions to users in the app.
03:21 Sonia Patel: Yes, we expose request-level traces and you can attach user identifiers in metadata. There's an optional prefix/KV cache behavior; note that cache can surface prior prompts if misused, but we can disable it for regulated flows.
03:37 Priya Nair: Good to know. For compliance we'll start with cache disabled.
03:42 Jordan Lee: Noted. We'll document that in the runbook.
03:46 Marco Alvarez: A practical question: what's the expected onboarding window? Our infra team can open a 4–6 hour maintenance window next Tuesday.
03:56 Alex Monroe: That should be enough for initial peering and smoke tests. The typical sequence is: network connectivity, key exchange for KMS, deploy small inference pool, run benchmark for 2–4 hours, then review.
04:12 Priya Nair: And who should we loop in on your side if we hit issues during the maintenance window?
04:18 Alex Monroe: Please include Sonia (SE) and Jordan (CSM) in the invite. We'll also have on-call infra if needed — we'll provide a contact.
04:27 Marco Alvarez: OK.
04:30 Sonia Patel: A couple of gotchas I've seen: firewall timeouts for long-lived KV cache connections and MTU mismatch on peering. We'll share a short checklist to avoid those.
04:41 Evelyn Chow: Also need to confirm data residency; our EU customers' data must stay in eu-central-1 region. Can you pin inference region?
04:50 Sonia Patel: Yes, we can pin the region. Private deployment can be deployed in your preferred region; hosted variants follow region placements too. We'll note that in the runbook.
05:02 Priya Nair: For the pilot success criteria, we propose: 1) verify connectivity and keys, 2) P95 latency < 350 ms for 64-token prompts, 3) cost estimate within 15% of target, and 4) no compliance blockers in audit logs.
05:17 Alex Monroe: That sounds like a good set. We'll add slight buffer on latency target in case of initial tunneling overhead.
05:24 Jordan Lee: I'll capture those as formal success criteria in the runbook and share.
05:30 Priya Nair: Timeline — can we aim to run the pilot by next Wednesday?
05:34 Alex Monroe: Yes, if we get CIDR ranges and security contact today or tomorrow, we can target next Wed for the run.
05:43 Marco Alvarez: I'll get the network details by EOD tomorrow.
05:46 Evelyn Chow: I'll confirm retention windows and what our legal needs to see.
05:51 Alex Monroe: Great. Any vendor concerns? Competitors?
05:55 Priya Nair: We'll also be evaluating an in-house self-host effort and Anthropic for certain workflows. Price and SLAs will be deciding factors.
06:06 Alex Monroe: Understood. We'll include a cost/comparison sheet and reference performance numbers.
06:12 Sonia Patel: For the benchmark we'll capture token cost, P50/P95 latencies, error rate, and trace logs. We'll give a spreadsheet so you can plug in your traffic mix.
06:26 Marco Alvarez: Is there a suggested sample prompt set you can provide to simulate our customer flows?
06:30 Sonia Patel: Yes, we'll attach a sample prompt set and a small harness script you can run from your side to generate load.
06:38 Priya Nair: One last operational question: who owns fielding support tickets during the pilot — Redwood or Bramble?
06:44 Jordan Lee: Redwood handles infra/perf bugs; Bramble handles application-level issues. We'll be triaging together and keep a shared ticket tracker.
06:52 Alex Monroe: OK, quick recap and actions — Alex to send SOC2 and security pack; Sonia to share benchmark plan and prompt set; Marco to provide network details; Evelyn to confirm retention; Jordan to draft runbook and schedule weekly check-ins. Any objections?
07:10 Priya Nair: No objections, sounds good.
07:14 Marco Alvarez: Good plan.
07:18 Evelyn Chow: Fine by me.
07:22 Alex Monroe: Great, we'll follow up in Slack and email. Thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.

End transcript.
